blocks.content:
The CAG can be removed in the SAME manner and on the SAME grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.

This means removal is done by the President after an address by both Houses of Parliament supported by a special majority on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity.
The CAG can be removed in the SAME manner and on the SAME grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.

items: CAG does NOT hold office during the pleasure of the President; guaranteed security of tenure exists.
Grounds for removal are strictly limited to 'proved misbehavior' or 'incapacity'—no other grounds are constitutionally valid.
Removal requires a 'Special Majority' (not simple majority) from BOTH Houses of Parliament before the President can issue the order.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CAG is removed in the exact same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
Removal requires an address passed by both Houses of Parliament.
Parliamentary address must be supported by a special majority.
Removal is formally executed by the President after parliamentary approval.
The only constitutional grounds for removal are proved misbehavior or incapacity.
